title: Placeus preferred — tenacious efficacious persuasion; Vermigli, Musculus, Le Blanc’s own formula
source_text: LXXXIX. Sed omnium commodissima, plenissima & brevissima simul, videtur definitio supra allata Josuae Placei, cui fides justificans est, Tenax & efficax persuasio veritatis eorum quae Verbo Dei nobis revelata sunt, speciatim vero promissionis de remissione peccatorum, & vita aeterna nobis per Christum parta. Nam cum dicit fidem illam esse persuasionem veritatis eorum quae Verbo Dei nobis revelata sunt, exprimit totum illud quod haec fides habet commune cum fide historica. Quum vero addit persuasionem illam esse tenacem atque efficacem, sub verbis istis complectitur totum illud quod fidem justificantem, ab historica, discernit atque discriminat. Cum Placei autem definitione coincidit jam ante memorata Petri Martyris descriptio, dum ait Fidem esse firmum certumque assensum Verbis Dei, a Spiritu Sancto afflatum, ad salutem credentium. Et assensum firmum exponit per eum, qui sit tantarum virium & efficaciae, ut secum trahat affectum fiduciae, spei, charitatis, & omnia tandem bona opera, ut praesentis vitae infirmitas patitur. Et etiam Musculi fidem definientis, Constantem assensum cordis ad ea quae vel narrantur, vel promittuntur verbo. Verbis meis dicerem fidem salutarem esse, assensum firmum, practicum, atque fiducialem adhibitum omnibus quae sunt a Deo revelata, speciatim autem promissionibus Evangelii.
pass_a_gloss: But of all the most convenient, fullest, and at the same time briefest, seems the definition of Joshua de la Place brought forward above, for whom justifying faith is, A tenacious and efficacious persuasion of the truth of those things which have been revealed to us by the Word of God, but specially of the promise of the remission of sins, and eternal life procured for us through Christ. For when he says that that faith is a persuasion of the truth of those things which have been revealed to us by the Word of God, he expresses all that this faith has in common with historical faith. But when he adds that that persuasion is tenacious and efficacious, under those words he embraces all that discerns and discriminates justifying faith from historical. But with Placeus's definition coincides the already before-mentioned description of Peter Martyr, when he says Faith is a firm and certain assent to the Words of God, breathed by the Holy Spirit, unto the salvation of believers. And he explains firm assent by that which is of such strength and efficacy that it draws with it the affection of trust, of hope, of charity, and at length all good works, as the infirmity of the present life allows. And also of Musculus defining faith, A constant assent of the heart to those things which are either narrated or promised by the word. In my own words I would say that saving faith is a firm, practical, and fiducial assent applied to all things which have been revealed by God, but specially to the promises of the Gospel.
pass_b_english: Le Blanc ranks Placeus’s definition most convenient, full, and brief: tenacious efficacious persuasion of what God reveals — specially remission and eternal life through Christ.
“Persuasion of revealed truth” marks what it shares with historical faith; “tenacious and efficacious” marks what sets justifying faith apart.
Vermigli: firm certain Spirit-breathed assent strong enough to draw fiducia, hope, charity, and good works.
Musculus: constant heart-assent to what the Word narrates or promises.
Le Blanc’s own: firm, practical, fiducial assent to all God reveals — specially Gospel promises.
